messages.author: 965db2f78ea93dc5
messages.subject: position_stack and variable widths
parts:
Hi,

I've been attempting to create a histogram with manual, non-uniform
breaks, using stat_bin's breaks parameter explicitly. The aesthetic
semantics of using varying binwidths may be questionable but it's what I
want nonetheless.

The above strategy works until I introduce an aes(fill=f) mapping, at
which point there is an implicit position_stack and I get the error
"Error: position_stack requires constant width".

Using position="identity" makes the error go away but just overplots the
bars. It's possible to construct the desired plot using geom_rect
instead of position_stack but it means a lot of tedious data processing
that ggplot should be doing itself.

I took a dive into the source code and found that the error is generated
in position-collide.r:

if (check.width && length(widths) > 1 && sd(widths) > 1e-6) {
stop(name, " requires constant width", call. = FALSE)
}

I think position_stack is a good candidate for doing what position_dodge
does and calling collide with check.width = FALSE. This has the desired
effect in my limited testing, and it seems that it shouldn't have
unintended effects, since the (internal) pos_stack function doesn't use
its width parameter at all!

I've attached a patch... or is there a better way of dealing with this?

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: position_stack and variable widths
parts:
Hi Dean,

That will work for this situation, but in general it might cause
problems, because the bars might have different locations in different
groups. This makes me a bit leery about taking the check away. The
real solution is to develop a stacking algorithm that works with
multiple widths, but I'm not sure where to start on that.

Hadley

You mean different x locations among the fill groups? Is this
something that wouldn't be caught by the intervals check?

> real solution is to develop a stacking algorithm that works with
> multiple widths, but I'm not sure where to start on that.

Well, the current stacking algorithm should work with anything
produced by stat_bin AFAICS. Are you looking for tetris-style
stacking? I could hack this out but such output seems pointless at
the data-presentation level. Do you have a test case in mind that
captures your intentions?

In the meantime, could we downgrade that stop to a warning? It's
getting in the way in the cases where the stacking algorithm *does*
work.
